_comment: Replace every value here. Nothing in this file is measured, and tierbook refuses to load it if you add a key that only a measurement may set.

reference-api.note: whatever you would send everything to if you were not routing

self-hosted.note: the hourly bill is required: a machine bills while idle, so without it the cost per request cannot be computed at all

_tenant_scope_note: tenant_scope is required on every family. 'single' is the template default because it is the common case and a legitimate declaration -- what tierbook refuses is silence about the tenant term SCOPE section 6's multiplicity family names, not the choice of 'single' itself. Change it to 'pooled' or 'per_tenant' if this family actually serves more than one tenant; neither is acted on yet, only recorded.
_label_source_note: label_source is oracle.kind's vocabulary (schema.json), read at load time, plus 'none'. 'none' is the template default because most deployments have not wired an online labeller yet -- replace it with whichever of the seven applies once one exists, set max_label_latency_s to a number (it must be null exactly when label_source is 'none'), and only then may this family carry an exploration_rate.
_staleness_limit_note: staleness_limit_days is required on every family. null here is the honest declaration of no stated limit -- this template family has no exploration_rate yet, so there is nothing for the limit to bound. Once this family declares an exploration_rate, staleness_limit_days must be a number: null combined with a rate is refused, because exploration exists to reach a candidate whose evidence has expired and an unbounded limit there is a bound from any past environment at all.
